title: The Plan That Didn't Happen
core_idea: Grieving a plan that never unfolded is natural; letting go of it frees attention for the life that is actually here.
text: There is a quiet kind of grief for plans that never happened. The trip you kept postponing. The house you pictured. The version of this year you were so sure about. Nobody sends flowers for a plan, so we often carry that loss alone. It helps to name it, gently: I really wanted that. Saying it out loud is not weakness. It is how the heart closes a chapter. And once it is named, something softens. Your attention, which was busy looking back at the road not taken, can turn toward the road beneath your feet. It may be different from the map. It is still yours.
description: A gentle reflection on grieving plans that never happened, and turning back toward the life that is here.
